paper.title: Interpolating Item and User Fairness in Multi-Sided Recommendations

settings.name_in_paper: Fair online recommendation (Problem FAIR, online setting, stochastic arrivals)
unmapped: N items (K arms), M user types observed as context, drawn i.i.d. with unknown probabilities p_j; binary purchase feedback with unknown probability y_{i,j} only for the offered item
reward is revenue r_i times purchase; the learner knows revenues r, the item outcome map L(theta), the item social welfare function W and the user outcome map U(theta)
item- and user-fairness constraints depend on the unknown instance and cannot be verified from feedback (uncertain constraints); fairness regret = max time-averaged constraint violation
benchmark is the optimum of the constrained Problem (FAIR) with fairness parameters delta^I, delta^U
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, some non-anticipating algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ generates the recommendation probabilities $\bm{x}_{t} \in \Delta_{N}^M$ ... After observing the type of the arriving user $J_t$, the platform offers item $i$ with probability $x_{t, i, J_t}$. Following this recommendation, the platform only observes the user's binary purchase decision $z_t \in \{0, 1\}$ for the offered item.

settings.name_in_paper: Fair online recommendation with periodic arrivals
unmapped: user-type arrival distributions p_t are periodic with period Q (p_{mQ+q} = p~^(q)); purchase probabilities fixed; benchmark uses the time-averaged arrival distribution; environment value nonstationary_switching is an approximation
the learner knows the period length Q
the learner knows revenues r, item outcome map L, item SWF W and user outcome map U
fairness constraints depend on the unknown instance and cannot be verified from feedback
settings.definition_quote: Consider a scenario where users arrive in each round $t\in [T]$ according to a probability distribution $\bm{p}_{t} \in \Delta_{M}$. Additionally, suppose that there exists a period length $\Period \in (0, T)$ and distributions $\widetilde{\bm{p}}^{(1)} \ldots \widetilde{\bm{p}}^{(\Period)}$ such that $\bm{p}_{m \Period + \period} = \widetilde{\bm{p}}^{(\period)}$

algorithms.name: FORM (Fair Online Recommendation algorithm for Multi-sided platforms)
FORM with sliding-window arrival estimates (periodic arrivals)

bound.regime: T sufficiently large: log(T) > max{(2+||r||_inf) B, 1/min_j p_j}

conditions: Assumption 1: local Lipschitzness of U(theta) and of the item-fair solution f^I(theta) with constant B in a neighborhood zeta

source.label: thm:stochaccuracy
source.quote: Given any problem instance $\bm{\theta} \in \Theta$ and assume that Assumption \ref{assum:lips} holds, for $T$ sufficiently large, we have that the revenue regret of \alg is at most $\E[\regr(T)] \leq \mathcal{O}(MN^{\frac{1}{3}}T^{-\frac{1}{3}})$; the fairness regret ... $\mathcal{O}(MN^{\frac{1}{3}}T^{-\frac{1}{3}})$.

results.notes: Paper's revenue regret is time-averaged (1/T sum of rev(x*)-rev(x_t)); multiplied by T. N items mapped to K, M user types to M_ctx. Regret is through expected revenues, so pseudo-regret against the optimum of the constrained Problem FAIR. Complete statement in appendix (thm:stochaccuracy-complete) gives the explicit large-T condition. Hidden constants depend on B, cutoff time, r.
